title: Eye Laser Cyberweapons
doc: Slice toggle. Off: Slices.VerdictForOverlay skips every file below before
it is opened, so none of its rows reach RulePlan. These files are loaded
by the row-edit engine, so they also have no effect while [Slices]
ModelRules is off (ModelRules.Init returns before Overlays.Load).
Files this toggle gates:
cyberweapons-lasers.csv
The 17 eye lasers: ImplantClass 32, ImplantSlot 8, WeaponClass 17
(Gear.WeaponClass.CyberWeaponEyes). Their install economics live in
implants-slot08.csv and their combat stats here. Cost appears in both
and means different things: the clinic price there, the item's
valuation here.
Lever sheet, not a direct overlay: the first column is WeaponName and
repeats (four each for Brightshot Optic, Lumen Spear, Photon Lance and
Helios Beam, then one Luem Trident). Cyberweapons.cs splits each row at
load into a WeaponModel rule and a TalentModel rule.
SpecialRule (WeaponModel) and ApCost (TalentModel) are levers on this
sheet although both are constant across the 17 game rows (SpecialRule 3,
ApCost 20) [measured, sheets/raw]. A column that is constant in the game
data can still carry a lever, so the usual "omit a constant column"
rule does not drop them (Cyberweapons.cs lever map).
REQUIRES Slices.ImplantsSlot08.
In the game data TalentModel has exactly 33 rows with a non-zero Weapon,
and each is pointed at by an ImplantModel row's ImplantTalentId: 17 from
ImplantClass 32 / ImplantSlot 8 (the eye lasers) and 16 from ImplantClass
27 / ImplantSlot 6 (the claws), with no other class or slot contributing
[measured, sheets/raw TalentModel.csv, ImplantModel.csv, WeaponModel.csv].
So the 17 rows here and 17 of the 18 ImplantClass 32 rows of
implants-slot08.csv are the same items. The 18th, ImplantTypeId 3217
"Lumen Trident", has ImplantTalentId 0 and so no laser row.
ImplantModel 3217 and 3218 are both named "Lumen Trident" while the
weapon, 25016, is "Luem Trident"; neither spelling is normalised.
[measured]
Brightshot Optic 1-4 are on both sheets (weapons 25000-25003, talents
80007-80010; ImplantTypeId 3200-3203, ImplantEffectId 50107-50110), and
both sheets carry a crit column for them against different tables: this
sheet's CritMultiBase/CritMultiStealth on WeaponModel, the slot-8
sheet's CritMultiBase on EffectModel. In the game data they are 4 of
the 9 implant effects with a non-zero CritMultiBase (25), all in slot 8
[measured, sheets/raw/EffectModel.csv]. With slot 8 off and lasers on,
the implant side keeps the game's value while this sheet's values
apply.
Rarity and PowerLevel also appear on both sides and differ: over the 33
paired items Rarity agrees on 17 and PowerLevel on 8 [measured]. What
either column does in the game is not established here.
check_schema.py evaluates the requires on the two .cfg keys. A run that
could not compare it prints a SKIPPED line and counts it on the
'requires:' census line.
